beats.headline: Intel climbs 11.4% amid broader chip rally
beats.explanation: Intel rose 11.42% to close at $58.95 on 1.8x average volume following an 8-K filing. The gain was shared with industry peers and suppliers, including equipment supplier ASML (+8.77%) and competitor AMD (+4.64%).

beats.headline: Intel surges 23.6% following Q1 10-Q filing
beats.explanation: Intel surged 23.60% to $82.54 with trading volume at 2.8x its 30-day average following the filing of its Form 10-Q and Form 8-K. Competitors also posted substantial moves, with AMD advancing 13.91% and QCOM gaining 11.12%.

beats.headline: Intel gains 12.1% on company-specific strength
beats.explanation: Intel jumped 12.10% to $94.75 on 2.3x normal volume without company-specific news in the record. The advance was largely company-specific, as competitor AMD rose a more moderate 4.30% while peers NVDA (-1.84%) and MSFT (-1.12%) declined.

beats.headline: Intel advances 12.9% across mixed peer group
beats.explanation: Intel shares rose 12.91% to cross $100 and reach $108.15 on 1.9x average volume with no specific filings or announcements. Peer performance was mixed: competitor QCOM rose 10.79% and supplier ASML gained 4.09%, while supplier and competitor TSM dropped 1.79%.

beats.headline: Intel rises 14.0% alongside competitor AMD
beats.explanation: Intel climbed 13.96% to finish at $124.92 on 2.2x normal volume with no company news provided. The rally was shared with competitor AMD (+11.44%) and competitor QCOM (+8.17%), while supplier and competitor TSM slid 0.60%.

beats.headline: Intel pulls back 5.1% in company-specific drop
beats.explanation: Intel dropped 5.14% to $114.68 on 1.9x average volume with no company-specific news reported. The move was company-specific, as competitor MSFT rose 5.45% and competitor AVGO advanced 4.73%, while competitor AMD fell just 0.38%.

beats.headline: Intel rebounds 11.2% alongside ASML and AMD
beats.explanation: Intel jumped 11.19% to $110.27 with volume at 1.3x average despite no company-specific catalysts. Supplier ASML (+6.54%) and competitor AMD (+5.13%) also advanced, whereas competitors AAPL (-1.89%) and GOOGL (-1.42%) declined.

beats.headline: Intel rises 9.3% in broader semiconductor push
beats.explanation: Intel shares climbed 9.27% to close at $116.96 on 1.9x typical trading volume without fresh company disclosures. The advance was shared across the sector, including supplier ASML (+9.53%), competitor AMD (+7.97%), and competitor QCOM (+6.15%).

beats.headline: Intel rallies 10.6% on broad industry strength
beats.explanation: Intel gained 10.64% to hit $133.99 on 2.3x normal volume with no company-specific updates. Strength was shared across the supply chain, as supplier and competitor TSM added 6.93%, competitor QCOM rose 6.17%, and competitor AMD climbed 4.86%.

beats.headline: Intel slides 9.7% alongside AMD and TSM
beats.explanation: Intel dropped 9.66% to $110.39 on 1.4x 30-day average volume in the absence of corporate news. The sell-off was shared with competitor AMD (-6.51%), supplier ASML (-4.26%), and supplier and competitor TSM (-4.25%).

beats.headline: Intel falls 7.9% after Q2 10-Q filing
beats.explanation: Intel shares decreased 7.89% to $92.32 on 1.8x typical volume following Form 8-K and 10-Q filings. The drop exceeded declines among peers, though competitor AMD fell 3.29% and supplier and competitor TSM dipped 2.93%.

beats.headline: Intel jumps 12.1% on AI CPU demand rally
beats.explanation: Intel gained 12.14% to $121.78 on 1.9x normal volume as enthusiasm around Meta's Muse AI agent fueled expectations for CPU demand. The rally lifted peer chipmakers as well, with competitor AMD jumping 9.95% to cross a $1 trillion market cap and competitor QCOM rising 9.29%.

arc: Between April and September 2026, Intel experienced sharp volatility driven by earnings reports and broader semiconductor sentiment, more than doubling from $52.91 to peaks above $133 before settling at $121.78. Strong upward momentum in late April was anchored by quarterly reporting, followed by a series of high-volume rallies in May and June that closely tracked movements in peers like AMD, ASML, and Qualcomm. A July contraction tied to second-quarter filings temporarily reversed these gains, but positive sentiment resurfaced in September as industry-wide demand drivers, including Meta's Muse AI agent, revitalized CPU interest across the chip sector.
